answers:
IBM Cloud enterprises enable you to manage multiple accounts within a single entity, offering centralized management and visibility. This structure helps organizations control costs, manage user access, and enforce security policies across all their IBM Cloud resources. 
If you're having difficulty accessing the entire enterprise, it may be due to restricted access to certain accounts rather than the whole enterprise account. In such cases, you can reach out to the enterprise owner to request appropriate access. If you are the owner, you can grant a user access to the entire enterprise through the IBM Cloud console.
IBM Cloud enterprises provide a framework for managing billing and resource usage across multiple accounts. Within an enterprise, you can create a multitiered hierarchy of accounts, with billing and payments managed at the enterprise level.
Additionally, IBM Cloud enterprises can be organized using resource groups and IAM (Identity and Access Management) access groups. Resource groups help you organize various services in your account into a common view and billing process. IAM access groups can be created for each team and assigned the necessary permissions to work with resources in a resource group, helping to minimize the number of IAM access policies you need to assign to individual users.
